<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx`  _(via email_template (literal, a string literal in BareNameRegistryType))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via email_template (literal, a string literal in BareNameRegistryType))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via email_template (literal, a string literal in BareNameRegistryType))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via email_template (literal, a string literal in BareNameRegistryType))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via email_template (literal, a string literal in BareNameRegistryType))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via email_template (literal, a string literal in BareNameRegistryType))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7189fb2a2f765b84c26c47e63f13adbb81f4d3da` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eff639863c43fcb67f2bdea461df91c0e9bde7fc` — the merge of head `a9d8e39701956668d5480cd984e9eb8de78d5093` into base `7189fb2a2f765b84c26c47e63f13adbb81f4d3da`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eff639863c43fcb67f2bdea461df91c0e9bde7fc && git checkout eff639863c43fcb67f2bdea461df91c0e9bde7fc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7189fb2a2f765b84c26c47e63f13adbb81f4d3da a9d8e39701956668d5480cd984e9eb8de78d5093 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7189fb2a2f765b84c26c47e63f13adbb81f4d3da && git merge --no-ff a9d8e39701956668d5480cd984e9eb8de78d5093

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7189fb2a2f765b84c26c47e63f13adbb81f4d3da
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7189fb2a2f765b84c26c47e63f13adbb81f4d3da` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `15ed46b6c2bd7d72e3747cf65ea5210eff96c9f1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0048-cross-package-metadata-collision.md + packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-ai-family.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-flow-family.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder-ai-family.dogfood.test.ts, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__objectql__src__bare-name-one-holder.ts.json (the changeset `.changeset/30803-bare-name-ai-family.md` is a prose face, read for ② only)

Two faces at once: the rules face (`docs/adr/0048-*.md` is the `reviewFace` hit) and the narrowing face (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Inputs: card #30803 (body, every comment, the rulings 6687840782 and 6688041914, the claim 6716532253, the os-dev-report 6717468349), PR #31375 (body, 9 files, commits `55c70231` + merge `15ed46b6`, net diff against merge base `e7354255`), PRs #30836 / #31006 / #31093 (merged), the check-runs on `15ed46b6`. Cited code read, never reviewed: `registry.ts` doors and seal, `engine-top-level.ts` collection loop, `spec/.../manifest-collection-spelling.ts`, `metadata-plugin.zod.ts`, `mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts`, `mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` (`agent_prompt`, skill bridge), `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` and `domains/ai.ts`, `rest` `/meta/:type/:name` through `SchemaRegistry.getItem`, `cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, `core/src/artifact-packages.ts`, ADR-0063 §2, hotcrm at `6961ab1` (read-only grep, no run).

Check-runs on `15ed46b6` at review time (the gate verdicts): completed success — Lint & Repo Gates (every `check:*` gate), Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · CI/release & engine gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped (all three), Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Plan Test Core shards. Still in progress — Test Core 1–8 and Type Check · workspace (the required `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` contexts). No failure. Two of the eleven required contexts are not complete, so this record is a contract verdict, not a green claim: the seat reads them to completion before landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The accept set**: `BARE_NAME_ONE_HOLDER_TYPES` grows 10 → 12 (`agent`, `skill` appended as the AI family), so the derived `BARE_NAME_REGISTRY_TYPES` grows 9 → 11 and `isBareNameOneHolderType` / `isBareNameRegistryType` answer true for both. Every door is generic over the list, so with no code change in `registry.ts` or `plugin.ts` (comments only, as the PR says — verified on the diff) three accept sets narrow after the seal: the package door (`refuseBareNameConflicts` over `declaredBareNames`, which now reads `agents` and `skills` on the manifest and each nested `plugins[]` entry one level deep), the item seam (`registerItem` with a `packageId`, type `agent` or `skill`), and the cold boot's seal (`sealBareNameHolders` iterates the list). **Right** — and reachable: the engine's collection loop registers `agents`, `tools`, `skills` (`METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS`, `engine-top-level.ts:4078`) through `registerItem` under the package's composite `PACKAGE:NAME` slot, and the spec's `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` folds `agents → agent`, `skills → skill`, so `COLLECTION_KEY` (`agents`, `skills`) names the keys the seams actually read.
- **Not bundled**: `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` holds only `email_template`, so `bundleBaseKey` is the identity for both types and the holder reading needs no member stripping. **Right**, and P1.9's "neither is bundled" is true.
- **Empty built-in and baseline sets** for both: `grep` over `packages/**` and `examples/**` finds no platform or example package declaring `agents:` or `skills:` (`packages/skills` is the SKILL.md catalog, not `skill` metadata; the open runtime answers `GET /ai/agents` with `{ agents: [] }`). **Right** for this repository. The `Record` type over `BareNameOneHolderType` makes both additions mandatory — the ablation's TS2322 confirms the type pins the list.
- **Refusal prose** (`CONSUMER_CLAUSE`, `TYPE_NOUN`, default `bareNameTypeLabel`): carries no tracker number, names the two consumers the measurement found. **Right**.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/objectql`**: nothing new on the index. `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` re-exports nothing from `bare-name-one-holder.ts` (the `declaredSecurityCatalogNames` export at line ~99 is the security catalog's, not this module's); the widened `BareNameRegistryType` union is module-internal. The published change is behavioural only: the doors' accept set. **Right**, and the `minor` level is for that.
- **Why the flow-family file moved**: its list cell pinned the WHOLE list with `toEqual`, which went red the moment a family appended; it now pins its own prefix (`slice(0, 10)`) and the AI family's file pins all twelve in order with `toEqual`. A pin that moves when the list grows is exactly what a whole-list pin in a non-last family is; the prefix pin still fails on a reorder or an insertion before the flow family, and the cell's second assertion (`BARE_NAME_REGISTRY_TYPES` = whole list minus `function`) still runs on the whole list. **Right**; no pin was weakened.
- **Dogfood door**: `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin` inline branch maps any `manifest.register` throw to `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` with the registry's sentence, and the registry refused ahead of every mutation, so "package list unchanged" is the right pin. **Right** (see ④ for the other branch).
- **Anchor JSON**: `adrs` unchanged, `invariant` restated with the fourth family and its served holder; `check-adr-anchors` needs a non-empty `adrs` and `invariant` and resolves the letter citations — `Lint · docs & code guards` is green on this head. **Right**.
- **Merge commit**: `git diff 55c70231 15ed46b6` over the PR's nine paths is empty, so the readings the report took on `55c70231` (full objectql suite, typechecks, ablation) describe this head's files; CI on `15ed46b6` covers the rest.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/30803-bare-name-ai-family.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`, title `feat(objectql)!:` — the same level and banner as PR 1–3's changesets (`30803-bare-name-one-package-holder.md`, `30803-bare-name-request-family.md`, `30803-bare-name-flow-family.md`, all still pending in `.changeset/`). Only `@objectstack/objectql` publishes from this diff (`@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true`; `scripts/`, `docs/` and the test files publish nothing). AGENTS.md's rule holds: a `narrowed` kind takes at least `minor`; the `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING and the body carries the BREAKING banner, Why / Before / Now / The cold boot / Who moves / Unchanged, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, PR 3's wording — right: no key, export or field is removed, no stored body changes shape; a refused name is renamed by its author). **Matches what the diff publishes.**
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — **right**: both doors refuse, after the seal, a registration they accepted on `main` (a second package's same-named agent or skill); no input is newly accepted anywhere in the diff.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — **right**: a package author's declarable set shrinks (a name another installed package holds is refused at install); the same declaration both PR 2 and PR 3 made for their families.
- `Skills-docs: none` — **right**: `skills/**` is untouched, and a grep of `skills/**` and `content/docs/**` finds no text teaching that two packages may ship a same-named skill or agent, nor any "unique within the package" guidance for either type. The spec's own words are "Skill unique identifier" / "Agent unique identifier" (`skill.zod.ts:298`, `agent.zod.ts:332`). The prescription lives in the refusal text and P1.9, as the series has done.
- Changeset "Measured producers": "HotCRM is not checked out in this container and is NOT MEASURED." It is checked out beside this repo: at hotcrm `6961ab1` there are six `*.skill.ts` (`customer_360`, `email_drafting`, `lead_qualification`, `live_data`, `revenue_forecasting` under `app.objectstack.hotcrm`; `case_triage` under `app.objectstack.hotcrm.service`) and no agent; all six names are distinct across its packages, so HotCRM holds no two-package clash and boots unwarned under this PR. The changeset's NOT MEASURED is honest, not wrong — **nit**: the seat may add this reading to the changeset or the PR when it next edits either; nothing blocks on it.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every deviation in report 6717468349, answered:

1. *Effort below the order's xhigh floor* — recorded on claim 6716532253; the seat's, not the tree's.
2. *Anchor JSON outside the claim's file surface* — the order names the anchor update; the invariant edit is one line and correct (①). Accepted.
3. *Flow-family list pin → `slice(0, 10)`* — judged in ①: right.
4. *Ablation DTS leg failed TS2322 after the JS bundles were written* — the expected consequence of filtering a literal out of a `Record`-pinned list; the marker was in 4 built files so the dogfood reading (3 of 4 red, CONTROL green) is of the mutated build. Accepted as a valid ablation.
5. *Gates re-run on `15ed46b6`, full suite / typecheck / ablation left on `55c70231`* — the merge touched none of the nine paths (①); CI on the head carries the typecheck and test families. Accepted.
6. *No labels on `pr_create`* — the auto-labeller has since set `documentation, size/l, tests, tooling`. Nothing owed.

Out-of-scope findings in the report, answered or escalated:

- **`tool` serves first-registered at `/meta/tool/NAME`, no warning, a third package installs `200` and is shadowed.** The ruling 6688041914 lists nine types and `tool` is not one; not adding it here is the right scope discipline, and the CONTROL pins (two packages' tools under one name both install after the seal) make the boundary explicit. But the measurement is a reproducible silent mis-resolution of the same class as the nine — Prime Directive 10 files such a thing, it does not leave it "noted". **Escalated to the seat**: file it as a card or put it on the maintainer's desk with phase 3 (#30806); the ruling's list is the maintainer's to extend. Not this PR's.
- **`ragPipelines` is not a `defineStack` key** (`StackSchema` refuses it) while the spec's `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` (`manifest-collection-spelling.ts:93`) and the engine's `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS` (`engine-top-level.ts:4078`) both list it — a collection declared in two registries that no author can reach. That is "declared ≠ enforced" (Prime Directive 10). **Escalated to the seat**: a card against `packages/spec` / `packages/objectql`, outside the ruling and this PR. P1.9's statement of it is accurate.
- **The kernel `metadata` service (`get('agent', NAME)`, the MCP `agent_prompt` read) lists no package agent on the composed runtime** while `/meta/agent/NAME` serves one — two by-name readers of one type disagree. Under ADR-0063 §2 agents are platform-owned and `*.agent.ts` is closed to third parties, so the metadata service's answer is the ADR's and the open `/meta` door is the generous one; the `StackSchema.agents` key (described "platform-internal") still registers a package's agents. Pre-existing, outside this PR; the narrowing is consistent with the ADR's direction either way. **Escalated to the seat** as a note for #30806 / the AI lane, not a blocker.
- **The cloud agent runtime, deployed and marketplace packages: NOT MEASURED** — stands. HotCRM, which the changeset also lists as unmeasured, is measured above (②): no clash.

**Tier H.** `docs/adr/0048-cross-package-metadata-collision.md` is a Tier H register row. `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` is `os-zhuang`, `hotlong`; the PR carries zero reviews at review time and is a draft. This record is a contract review, not that approval: an authorized APPROVED review from one of the two must exist, undismissed, before the owning seat lands it through the queue (the maintainer's merge or enqueue is the other landing). `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green, which is the guard's own reading at PR time, not a substitute for the approval.

### ④ Design judgment

**The ADR-0048 changes, against their first consumers and the rulings.**

- *Header Addenda line* — adds "agents and skills — phase 1 complete"; the anchor link is unchanged and still resolves to the addendum heading. Holds.
- *§3.4 note (2026-11-06)* — adds `/meta/agent/NAME` and "an MCP client's skill prompt" to the consumer list, "agent or skill" to the refused list, drops the "to follow" sentence and adds "a `tool` among them" to what keeps §3.4. Each clause holds against the code read: `/meta/:type/:name` ends in `SchemaRegistry.getItem(type, name)` with no package, which answers the bare slot, then the first composite slot in insertion order (`registry.ts:8123–8150`) — the first-registered package; `listSkillPrompts` keeps the first row per name and drops the rest (`skill-prompts.ts`), over the merged `skill` listing both the HTTP (`runtime/domains/mcp.ts`, `readMergedSkillRows`) and stdio (`mcp-server-runtime.ts`, `mergedDiagnosedList`) bridges read. **Should-fix (prose, nit-grade on the contract)**: "Every other type, a `tool` among them, an action bound to an object among them, keeps §3.4 as written" stacks two "among them" clauses in one sentence; one of them wants to go ("Every other type — a `tool`, an action bound to an object — keeps §3.4 as written"). No effect on the rule; fix in the next ADR touch or now, the seat's call.
- *Status line* — "P1.2, P1.7, P1.8, P1.9 — the last". Holds.
- *P1.5 "The series, complete"* — records the four families and their sections; "the data family (P1.1)" points at the measurement section rather than the refusal (P1.2) — harmless, the heading says "complete" and the body names P1.9 as the close. Holds against the ruling 6688041914 (PR order; all nine kept in #30803).
- *P1.9* — the measurement (both orders, a third package after the boot), what is refused ("the same two doors, the same holders, the same envelope and rename"; "neither is bundled", no baseline or built-in; agent and skill never meet), what is not in the list (`tool` with its measurement; `rag_pipeline` undeclarable), the cold boot under P1.3's `'warn'`, and the close. Every claim matches `bare-name-one-holder.ts` after the diff, the registry seams, and the AI-family pins; the first consumer (the list and the anchor invariant) agrees with the text. P1.6 "Where it is implemented" stays true unchanged. Holds.
- *Cold boot B* — `BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE` untouched at `'warn'`; the seal still fires at `kernel:bootstrapped` after the install-local rehydrate at `kernel:ready` (`plugin.ts:1229`). The unit cells pin one warning line naming both holders and the rename and the "changes nothing about which holder each caller is served" sentence; the dogfood pins the `WARN` level on a booted showcase. Ruling 6687840782 honoured.

**The narrowing itself, against the published spec on `main`.** It makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away. On `main` ADR-0048 P1.5 already names `agent` and `skill` as "to follow in the series' last change", the ruling kept both in the card, and the spec calls each name a "unique identifier"; the two consumers that exist in the open framework are name-keyed with no package. Two packages shipping one agent or skill name was never a declared capability — it was a silent mis-serve of one of them. Break attempts:

- *Both orders*: holders are a set over the item store's composite slots plus install claims, read per `(type, name)`; the refusal lists every holder (the cold-boot test pins `alpha` then `beta` as `existingHolder` rows). Order does not matter to the refusal. Holds.
- *A third package after the boot*: refused at the package door naming both, nothing recorded (unit); `install-local` inline → `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED`, package list unchanged, readers untouched (dogfood). Holds.
- *The package door vs the item seam*: a nested plugin's collections and a direct package-bound `registerItem` both hit the seam; pinned. The environment slot (no `packageId`) is never judged — and for these two types the protocol door already closes an environment overlay of a package-shipped item (`allowEnvironmentOverlay: false` for `agent`, `skill`, `tool` in `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY`), so the registry-level CONTROL is correct and, at the protocol door, moot. Holds.
- *Cold-boot warn vs post-seal refuse*: warn at boot, refuse after; `'refuse'` refuses the boot with the doors' envelope; a reload keeps both holders. Pinned. Holds.
- *Built-in or baseline items shipped by the platform*: none in this repository (①). In cloud, `service-ai` resolves the two platform agents (`ask`, `build`, ADR-0063 §2); if it registers them as `agent` items under its own package id, an app shipping an agent named `ask` is refused after the seal — which is what ADR-0063 wants (agents are closed to third parties), not a wrong refusal; at a cold boot it would warn, as today's `/meta/agent/ask` already serves the first-registered. NOT MEASURED (cloud), noted, not a finding against this tree.
- *An `agent` and a `skill` sharing one name*: separate type maps, separate claim maps; CONTROL pin. Holds.
- *Install-local — the cloud-fetched branch.* **Should-fix, out of this diff, series-wide, carrier: the seat as a card.** `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` has two branches around `manifest.register`: the inline-manifest branch refuses every throw as `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` (what the dogfood pins, for all four families); the `{ packageId, versionId }` branch (manifest fetched from the marketplace) stays lenient by design (#22695) and refuses only a `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` whose `conflicts[]` names an **environment** holder (`refusesEnvironmentHeldCatalogName`, #25366) — any other throw, a `BareNameConflictError` naming a **package** holder included, is logged as "hot-register failed (will load on next restart)", the ledger entry is written, the answer is a success with `hotLoaded: false`, and at the next boot the package rehydrates BEFORE the seal, where the clash becomes a cold-boot WARN and both packages hold the name. On that branch "refused at managed install" is not real for any of the eleven registry types — this PR's two included — and the "will load on next restart" sentence is literally true and semantically the bypass. This is not this PR's hunk: the branch predates the series, PR 1–3 shipped the same door and the same claim, and the fix is one predicate in `cloud-connection` (treat a `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` with `conflicts[]` of any holder kind as the pre-write refusal it is — a restart heals a package-held clash no more than an environment-held one; it only downgrades it to a warning), not a change to the list. The PR's own hunks are correct and the inline door, the item seam and the cold boot are all real, so this does not fail the tree; it does need a card before anyone reads P1.2/P1.9's "managed install" as covering both branches. Prime Directive 10 names the remedy (file it; keep the claim as narrow as the enforcement).
- *Spec-level naming* — a `SkillSchema`/`AgentSchema` name regex of `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$` admits an unprefixed name; the namespace rule is phase 2/3 (#30805, #30806). Out of scope here by the ruling's phasing; the refusal's rename (`NAMESPACE_NAME`) points at it.

**Series convention**: a fourth per-family test file and dogfood file rather than a `describe` in the data family's harness file — AGENTS.md (ruling record 6583487846) prefers the shared harness, but PR 2 and PR 3 established one file per family under contract review; **nit**, consistent with the series.

**Findings, graded.** Must-fix: none. Should-fix: (a) the cloud-fetched `install-local` branch swallows a package-held `BareNameConflictError` into the lenient restart path — card against `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, series-wide, not this PR's hunk; (b) the §3.4 note's doubled "among them" clause — prose. Nits: HotCRM reading for the changeset's producers line; the per-family test file against the shared-harness rule. Out-of-scope, escalated to the seat: `tool` (same defect class, outside the ruling — maintainer's list), `ragPipelines` (declared in two tables, reachable from neither), the `agent_prompt` / `/meta/agent` reader disagreement.
